name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 138 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Tamil Nadu.
status.nb: 138 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Tamil Nadu.

summary.en: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir are pursuing 65 foreign terrorists while the Union Home Secretary and the IB Director are scheduled to visit for a security review. In Manipur, spurious liquor deaths have risen to 20 and nine arrested persons remain in police custody. In Chhattisgarh, authorities seized a cash dump of 39.77 lakh rupees and Maoist weapons and two Maoists surrendered after a bounty was placed on one. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrkene i Jammu og Kashmir forfølger 65 utenlandske terrorister mens Unionens hjemdepartementssekretær og IB-direktøren er planlagt å besøke for en sikkerhetsgjennomgang. I Manipur har dødsfall knyttet til falsk alkohol steget til 20, og ni arresterte personer forblir i politiets varetekt. I Chhattisgarh konfiskerte myndighetene en kontantdump på 39.77 lakh rupees og maoistvåpen, og to maoister overgav seg etter at det ble satt en dusør på en av dem. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
